title: Engineer Fast Pilot Play Brief
content:
Deck purpose: enable SEs/SDRs to run a tight 30–40 minute technical demo that converts engineering teams into a 2–4 week pilot with clear success metrics.

Audience: integration/platform engineers, infra architects, ML infra leads. Assumes they already did an initial discovery call; this play gets them to a pilot commitment.

Play length: 30 minutes demo + 10 minutes Q&A + immediate pilot sheet handoff.

Slide 1 — One-line opener
- One-liner to say aloud: "Redwood delivers predictable inference economics and SLA-backed performance so your team can ship LLM features without building the serving stack."
- Rapid value hook: 2–3 min: show latency + cost delta for a real customer use case (search rerank).

Slide 2 — Persona quick-check (speaker note)
- Who we want in the room: infra lead (latency/cost), ML eng (validation/quality), product (success metrics).
- Ask: Which of these three are you most concerned about?

Slide 3 — Pilot proposition (core offer)
- 2–4 week pilot: sandboxed model serving, per-route observability, canary rollout, and a simple billing estimate.
- Deliverables: dedicated trial capacity, SLO targets agreed, one integration pattern (API embed or private VPC), weekly checkpoints.

Slide 4 — Minimal technical checklist (prep before demo)
- Sample prompt corpus or representative traffic (10–50 queries).
- Target latency SLO (p50/p95) and cost constraints.
- Data privacy requirement (PII?/on-prem?/VPC).
- Access: temporary API key + optional VPC peering details.

Slide 5 — Demo script (30 minutes)
- 0–3 min: quick context, restate goals and pilot definition.
- 3–8 min: show Console -> Model catalog -> Select model -> streaming response. Keep it fast — latency numbers visually visible.
- 8–15 min: Infra demo: Dedicated pool config, autoscale policy, canary rollout UI, fallback routing policy.
- 15–22 min: Observability: token breakdown, per-route traces, error heatmap, quality regression alert example.
- 22–28 min: Integration snippets: SDK call, streaming hook, caching config. Paste minimal curl and Python snippet.
- 28–30 min: Pilot commitment slide, next steps.

Slide 6 — Common engineering objections + suggested responses
- Objection: "We can self-host and control costs" -> Response: "You can, but compare ramp time, maintenance & ops cost. We give predictable throughput and kernel optimizations out of the box; we can hand off a Private deployment later."
- Objection: "Latency spikes on tail" -> Response: "We use continuous batching + smart routing and KV cache warmup; show p95 chart and fallback to smaller-quantized model."
- Objection: "Model quality drift" -> Response: "We bundle eval hooks and regression alerts and let you pin model versions with canary rollouts."

Slide 7 — Rapid fallback play (for live pilot incidents)
- If p95 breach: 1) divert traffic to lower-latency variant, 2) enable shorter seq-length quantized profile, 3) notify on-call + open rollback.
- Script for SEs: run fallback command in Console -> confirm traffic shift -> email template to stakeholders (see template below).

Slide 8 — Pilot SLOs & success criteria (agree before kickoff)
- Latency: p50 target, p95 target (numbers set per customer).
- Cost: cost-per-1k tokens relative to baseline.
- Quality: accuracy on holdout prompt set (pass threshold).
- Integration: SDK deployed to staging endpoint and 95% of test prompts passed.

Slide 9 — Pricing anchor for pilot conversion conversation
- Trial covers infra + 1 week of SE support. Typical conversion anchors: expected monthly tokens -> suggested Dedicated commit band with cost savings 20–35% vs hosted.
- Quote example (speaker): "Expect 2–4x per-token cost reduction when moving to reserved, with <6 week ROI for medium traffic pilots."

Slide 10 — Playbook: immediate follow-up artifacts (after demo)
- Send pilot kickoff packet (template included below), include: pilot charter, sample prompts, SLO sheet, contact list, calendar invites for weekly syncs.
- Attach a sandbox API key and a short runbook for basic troubleshooting.

Appendix A — Email templates (copy/paste)
- Pilot kickoff email subject: "[Pilot] Redwood + <Customer> — kickoff & SLOs"
- Body: short bullets: objectives, timeline, SLOs, keys, next sync time, link to status doc.

Appendix B — Quick rollback email (if breach)
- Subject: "Action: Pilot traffic rollback to variant B — immediate"
- Body: what changed, who toggled, expected effect, timestamp, next steps.

Appendix C — Demo artifacts to attach in drive (pre-built)
- Minimal curl + Python snippets, 10-sample prompt corpus, SLO template spreadsheet, pilot kickoff checklist.

Speaker notes: keep language engineer-friendly, keep claims quantifiable (show numbers/charts where possible), and always ask for a concrete next step (dates + ownership).

Open questions (to finalize before next iteration):
- Do we include a short latency/cost calculator embedded in the deck? (pros: fast anchor; cons: complexity)
- Should we produce a separate variant for regulated industries (compliance-first talking points)?

Version history: v0.1 brainstorm 2024-11-04; v0.2 consolidated 2025-01-22; v0.3 this doc 2025-02-18 (in review).

Checklist before publishing as field-ready:
- [ ] final slide screenshots from Console (no PII)
- [ ] link to pilot billing template and legal starter contract
- [ ] SE rehearsal notes and role assignments
- [ ] copy review by product for accuracy

Notes-to-self: keep the deck short, skip deep-architecture slides unless asked; we want commitment to a pilot, not to design the full production topology in the first meeting.

End of play brief.
